summary.headline: KPIT Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.5% YoY in rupee terms (0.2% YoY in CC) as off-highway and CV grew 27% YoY, offsetting a 13%+ revenue drop from two top OEMs.
summary.overview: Management said Q2 was in line with its own expectations, with growth of 6.5% YoY and 1% QoQ in rupee terms, and 0.5% QoQ and 0.2% YoY in constant currency. Passenger car revenue fell about 8% YoY and 4% QoQ, driven by sharp declines at two top accounts (one in Japan, one in Europe) that together were 13% of total revenue. Off-highway and commercial vehicles grew 27% YoY and 17.6% QoQ, and Products revenue grew 5% QoQ and 25% YoY. EBITDA margin rose 60 bps to 17.8% on mix, while net cash fell to about INR 6.2 billion on dividends, the Cymotive payment and a DSO increase from 51 to 53 days.

segments.name: Passenger car
segments.commentary: Down about 8% YoY and 4% QoQ; excluding the two top accounts (13% of revenue) the decline was absorbed by off-highway, CV and Products growth. Management expects the two accounts to bottom out over the next couple of quarters.

segments.name: Off-highway and commercial vehicles
segments.commentary: Grew 27% YoY and 17.6% QoQ. Off-highway has 3 clients with 2 more being added; SDM consulting engagements rose to 3 (one program launch expected next year per Korea comment).

segments.name: Products
segments.commentary: Grew 5% QoQ and 25% YoY; management will share product revenue more fully next year, with detailed reporting possibly early next year.

segments.name: Geographies
segments.commentary: Europe and Japan declined on the two OEM exits; Americas grew QoQ and YoY; SIMA (now split from Asia) grew, led by India. Vietnam investment being doubled for a Chinese Tier 1 centre and an existing OEM.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 expected to be better than H1, reiterated; growth expected in Q4 but no numbers given.
The two top OEM accounts expected to bottom out in the next couple of quarters, with gradual recovery into early next year.
European OEM consolidation expected to be meaningfully concluded by end of Q1 FY28; impact in H1 next year.
EBITDA expected to rise every quarter, with return toward the earlier 20-21% range only early next year.
QORIX programs pushed out: Gen 4 programs moved from 2028 to 2029-30; no stabilisation timeline given.
capex_capacity: R&D spend increased by a couple of million dollars QoQ in the quarter.
Vietnam subsidiary being scaled up, including a centre with a large Chinese Tier 1 to deliver China OEM global programs outside China.
Cost mix may shift from high-cost to low-cost centres as clients move to remote delivery; technology investment teams will not be optimised.
Energytech and deep-tech adjacency offerings being built; early wins expected in 2-3 quarters, meaningful impact takes longer.
demand_pricing: Wins were mainly in Autonomy, Connected and IDART; 89% of wins came from target accounts.
Passenger car weakness at two OEMs (Japan and Europe) with cancelled programs or cut spend; European passenger car OEMs cutting costs and sourcing from India.
Trucks in North America showing signs of growth; off-highway expected to keep growing; European PASSCAR OEMs still struggling.
AI platform: over 9,000 users, 5 million+ transactions and 12,000 engineering agents built in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Are the two large customer declines bottoming, and can Asia and Europe recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Sachin Tikekar said both OEMs (one in Japan under JKC, one in Europe) should bottom out in the next couple of quarters, with gradual growth returning early next year; Americas grew and India drove SIMA growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cash flow decline in H1 due to working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Priya Hardikar cited dividend, Cymotive acquisition payment and higher DSO, which lifted the working capital cycle; she did not quantify the cash conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to 20-21% EBITDA as growth accelerates?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said margins will rise somewhat every quarter, with a return toward earlier levels only early next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the CV segment's growth broad-based and sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said off-highway is concentrated on 3 clients but broadening with 2 more being added, and trucks should pick up in coming quarters on North America recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QORIX outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said programs were pushed out by a couple of years; Anup Sable said Gen 4 programs moved from 2028 to 2029-30, and management is exploring adjacencies such as robotics and more partners.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee costs rise in line with revenue given fixed-price growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Kishor Patil said AI leverage and products/solutions growth will drive operating leverage, but not across all clients; headcount additions depend on client adaptability.

risks_watch: Continued weakness at the two top OEMs (about 13% of revenue) beyond the expected two-quarter bottoming.
Attrition rose to mid-teens in Q2; management expects it to fall substantially next quarter after increments.
Working capital pressure: DSO rose to 53 days and operating cash flow conversion fell in H1 (analyst cited about 57% vs 75-80% last year).
QORIX losses and delayed Gen 4 programs with no stabilisation timeline.
Whether Q4 growth materialises, as no numbers were given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and AI differentiation, but cautious on near-term passenger car recovery; repeatedly declined to give numbers on H2 growth, QORIX timing or margin recovery, and framed the two-OEM decline as bottoming in a couple of quarters.
key_quotes: So overall growth has been 6.5% year-on-year and 1%, in terms of quarter-on-quarter, in rupee terms.
So absolutely, there is such opportunity.
We expect growth, and we will not be in a position to put any numbers now, but we expect growth in that quarter.
